title: Toy instrument (engine regression test only)
source: Synthetic — not a real psychometric instrument.

sections.body: A synthetic instrument used to regression-test the scoring engine. Two facets roll up into one domain; one item per facet is reverse-keyed.

items.text: I expect good things to happen.
I dwell on what might go wrong.
I stay relaxed when things get tense.

scales.name: Wellbeing
scales.construct_explainer: Wellbeing here groups two related tendencies; the score reflects how the answers lean across both facets.

low.shadow: Answers may lean toward a heavier load.
low.one_thing_to_try: Name one thing that went well today.

balanced.shadow: Can swing either way under pressure.
balanced.one_thing_to_try: Notice which facet pulls hardest this week.

high.shadow: Steady answers can mask real stress.
high.one_thing_to_try: Check whether the steadiness is real or rehearsed.

scales.name: Optimism
scales.construct_explainer: Optimism reflects a tendency to expect favourable outcomes.

low.shadow: Answers may lean toward expecting the worst.

balanced.shadow: May hesitate when a call is needed.
balanced.one_thing_to_try: Pick the more hopeful read once this week.

high.shadow: Hope can skip over real risks.
high.one_thing_to_try: Name one risk you might be glossing over.

scales.name: Calm
scales.construct_explainer: Calm reflects a tendency to stay settled when conditions get tense.

low.shadow: Answers may lean toward easily rattled.
low.one_thing_to_try: Try one slow breath before reacting.

balanced.shadow: Can tip either way on a hard day.
balanced.one_thing_to_try: Notice the earliest sign of tension.

high.shadow: Settled answers can hide a real signal.
high.one_thing_to_try: Ask whether calm is helping or avoiding.

sections.prompt: Which of these tendencies fits, and which does not? What is one thing you will try?
